fatal_errors: The proposed system is passivated Q235 steel, whereas the target study concerns an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L followed by annealing.
It omits the central intervention: approximately 150 µm HEA coating deposition and comparison of as-sprayed and 400–850 °C annealed states, particularly the 550 °C optimum.

The cited evidence establishes time-dependent degradation of passivated Q235 during ambient cyclic salt spray, not film failure at 700–900 °C; the high-temperature mechanism is therefore an unsupported extrapolation.
The experiment changes both temperature and exposure mode, comparing room-temperature salt spray with an unspecified high-temperature salt environment, so temperature is not cleanly isolated.

The predicted high-temperature weight loss conflicts with the target measurements, which use cyclic weight gain from oxide-scale formation and report reduced weight gain for the coated, 550 °C-annealed specimen.
explanation: The hypothesis is testable and includes boundaries and a falsification rule, but it reconstructs a different material system and mechanism. Its evidence appropriately supports early protection, rupture, rust-layer evolution, and eventual loss of passivation for Q235 under ambient accelerated salt spray. It does not support the asserted thermal-stress/chloride-diffusion transition at 700–900 °C. The target instead attributes improved electrochemical and 900 °C hot-corrosion behavior to an AlCoCrFeNi coating, 550 °C annealing-induced densification and grain refinement, retained BCC/FCC structure, and Al/Cr-rich passive oxides, with eventual ingress through coating pores and cracks. A discriminating design would require coated and uncoated SS316L, as-sprayed and annealed controls, fixed salt compositions, electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt% H2SO4, and cyclic 900 °C mass-gain and post-corrosion phase/microstructure measurements.
